findings.name: Disabled Veteran Homestead Property Tax Exemption
findings.description: In addition to Louisiana's standard $7,500 homestead exemption, veterans with a VA service-connected disability rating of 50-69% receive an additional $2,500 exemption of assessed valuation; veterans rated 70-99% receive an additional $4,500 exemption of assessed valuation; and veterans rated 100% (including 100% unemployability/IU) are exempt from ad valorem taxation on the entire remaining assessed value of their homestead-exempt property. An eligible unmarried surviving spouse of a veteran who was 100% disabled/unemployable may retain the full exemption if they continue to own and occupy the property.
findings.value: $2,500 additional exemption (50-69% rating); $4,500 additional exemption (70-99% rating); full exemption of remaining assessed value beyond the $7,500 homestead exemption (100%/unemployability rating)
otherReqs: Property must be owned and occupied as the veteran's homestead
Must already be receiving the standard homestead exemption
Apply through the parish assessor's office
Surviving spouse of a 100%/unemployable veteran may retain the exemption if unmarried and remains owner-occupant
findings.agency: Louisiana Parish Tax Assessors / Louisiana Department of Veterans Affairs
documentation: VA disability rating letter confirming service-connected disability percentage
Proof of homestead exemption already on file with the parish assessor
findings.sourceExcerpt: the next four thousand five hundred dollars of the assessed valuation of property owned and occupied by a veteran with a service-connected disability rating of seventy percent or more but less than one hundred percent by the United States Department of Veterans Affairs shall be exempt from ad valorem taxation... the remaining assessed valuation of property receiving the homestead exemption that is owned and occupied by a veteran with a service-connected disability rating of one hundred percent unemployability or totally disabled... shall be exempt from ad valorem taxation.

findings.name: Louisiana State Veterans Homes
findings.description: Louisiana operates five state veterans homes: the Louisiana Veterans Home in Jackson (East Feliciana Parish), Northeast Louisiana Veterans Home in Monroe, Northwest Louisiana Veterans Home in Bossier City, Southwest Louisiana Veterans Home in Jennings, and Southeast Louisiana Veterans Home in Reserve. Eligible residents include honorably discharged veterans (wartime or peacetime, at least 90 days active duty), spouses of veterans, and Gold Star parents. The fetched homepage indicated cost varies by disability rating (described as free for veterans with a 70%+ VA disability rating, with a monthly fee cited for those below that threshold and a separate monthly fee for spouses/Gold Star parents) but these specific dollar figures were paraphrased by the fetch tool rather than quoted verbatim from the page, so they should be re-confirmed directly with LDVA or a specific home before being presented as exact figures.
findings.value: Long-term/nursing care; admission cost reduced or waived based on VA disability rating (exact current fee schedule not independently verified this session)
otherReqs: Honorably discharged, wartime or peacetime service
Served at least 90 days active duty (or eligible National Guard/Reservist)
Spouses of veterans and Gold Star parents also eligible
Admissions application required
documentation: DD-214 or other proof of discharge
VA disability rating letter (for fee determination)
findings.sourceExcerpt: Veterans Assistance Counselors on Staff to Work with Veterans Regarding Their Benefits... Memory Care Wing for Alzheimer's or Dementia-Related Diagnoses

findings.name: Title 29 Fee Exemption for Dependents of Disabled/Deceased Veterans
findings.description: Louisiana's Title 29 program exempts eligible children and spouses of qualifying veterans from tuition and school-imposed fees (not student-imposed fees) at Louisiana public postsecondary institutions. Per the LDVA page fetched this session, eligibility categories are: children of living qualifying veterans; spouses of POW/MIA veterans; and surviving spouses and children of deceased veterans. Secondary university financial-aid sources (LSU, not a .gov domain) state the living-veteran threshold is a 90%+ service-connected disability rating or 100% individual unemployability, and cite a 4-years-of-schooling-within-5-years or age-25 limit for children with no age limit for surviving spouses, plus a Louisiana residency/driver's-license requirement and a 2.0 GPA/full-time enrollment standard. I could not independently confirm the exact 90% threshold, GPA requirement, or full statutory text against a primary Louisiana Legislature (legis.la.gov) page this session — a legis.la.gov lookup returned an adjacent statute (R.S. 29:290) rather than R.S. 29:288 itself, and law.justia.com returned a 403 error. Treat the 90% figure and residency/GPA specifics as reported-but-unverified pending confirmation directly against R.S. 29:288 text or an LDVA-issued eligibility document.
findings.value: Exemption from tuition, matriculation, registration, laboratory, athletic, medical, and other school-imposed fees (student-imposed fees excluded) at Louisiana public postsecondary institutions
otherReqs: Children ages 16-25 generally; benefit good for 4 years of schooling completed within 5 years or until age 25
No age limit cited for surviving spouses
Apply through parish veterans service office for a Fee Exemption Certificate
Full-time enrollment reportedly required (not independently verified)
findings.agency: Louisiana Department of Veterans Affairs / Louisiana public postsecondary institutions
documentation: VA disability rating letter or death/KIA documentation for the veteran
Proof of relationship (birth or marriage certificate)
findings.legalCitation: La. R.S. 29:288 (not independently confirmed against primary statute text this session)
findings.sourceExcerpt: For living veterans, children are eligible; for veterans who are POW/MIA, spouses are eligible; and for deceased veterans, surviving spouses and children are eligible.

findings.name: Veterans' Preference in State Civil Service Hiring
findings.description: Louisiana State Civil Service adds preference points to the passing examination score of eligible veteran applicants for original appointments (not promotions). The official HR Handbook page confirms a five-or-ten-point preference system exists. Secondary sources (not independently confirmed against the primary procedure document, which returned corrupted/unreadable PDF content when fetched this session) report the split is 5 points for honorably discharged non-disabled veterans and 10 points for veterans with a VA-established service-connected disability, and that the preference extends to a veteran's spouse, surviving spouse, or surviving parent in certain circumstances.
findings.value: 5 or 10 preference points added to civil service exam score for original appointment (exact disability-linked split not independently verified this session)
otherReqs: Honorable discharge required
Applies only to original appointment, not promotions
Preference may extend to spouse, surviving spouse, or surviving parent of a qualifying veteran
Submit DD-214 (and current VA disability letter if claiming disability-based points)
findings.agency: Louisiana Department of State Civil Service
findings.form: SF-11 Claim Form for Veterans Preference
findings.sourceExcerpt: eligible applicants who meet minimum qualifications and testing requirements shall have five or ten points added to their final examination score for veterans' preferences.

findings.name: Disabled Veteran Military Honor License Plate
findings.description: Louisiana resident veterans with a VA service-connected disability rating of 50% or more are eligible for a free 'DV' military honor license plate under R.S. 47:490.4, restricted to passenger cars, pickup trucks, recreational vehicles, motorcycles, and vans. A related plate under R.S. 47:490.32 is available to Purple Heart recipients who are also qualified disabled veterans (also requiring a 50%+ rating), printed 'Purple Heart Disabled Veteran.' Both plates are issued with no fee and are exempt from the renewal requirements that apply to standard plates; holders may also receive a free accessibility hang tag.
findings.value: Free license plate (no purchase or renewal fee) plus optional free accessibility hang tag
otherReqs: Service-connected disability rating of 50% or more from the VA
Louisiana resident
Restricted to passenger cars, pickup trucks, RVs, motorcycles, and vans
One plate issuable per vehicle registered in the applicant's name
Purple Heart recipients with a 50%+ rating may instead request the Purple Heart-specific variant
findings.agency: Louisiana Office of Motor Vehicles (Department of Public Safety)
documentation: VA disability rating letter confirming 50%+ service-connected disability
findings.legalCitation: La. R.S. 47:490.4 (general disabled veteran plate); La. R.S. 47:490.32 (Purple Heart disabled veteran plate)
findings.sourceExcerpt: a qualified disabled veteran shall include any veteran who has a service-connected disability of fifty percent or more and who is a resident of this state... No fee shall be charged for the license plates authorized by this Section and such plates shall not be subject to the renewal requirements applicable to standard plates.

findings.name: Disabled Veteran Hunting and Fishing License
findings.description: Veterans with a permanent service-connected disability rating of 50% or more are eligible for a free combination hunting and fishing license package from the Louisiana Department of Wildlife and Fisheries. The $4 fee otherwise charged is covered by the Louisiana Wildlife and Fisheries Foundation, not waived by statute directly. It is unclear from the fetched source whether this specific free-license tier is limited to Louisiana residents (a separate, less-generous 80%-discounted combo license is explicitly described elsewhere as for honorably discharged veteran residents), so residency requirements for this particular license should be confirmed before being treated as certain.
findings.value: Free combo license covering Basic and Saltwater Fishing Licenses; Basic, Deer, Waterfowl, and Turkey Hunting Licenses; and the WMA Access Permit (Federal Duck Stamp not included)
otherReqs: Disability must be classified as permanent
Does not include the Federal Duck Stamp
Apply in person at LDWF Headquarters, by mail, or by email with required documentation
findings.agency: Louisiana Department of Wildlife and Fisheries
documentation: VA disability rating letter confirming permanent 50%+ service-connected disability
findings.sourceExcerpt: For veterans who have a permanent service-connected disability classification of 50% or more... The Louisiana Wildlife and Fisheries Foundation covers the $4 fee for this license... Includes Basic and Saltwater Fishing Licenses; Basic, Deer, Waterfowl, and Turkey Hunting Licenses; and the WMA Access Permit... Does not include the Federal Duck Stamp.

findings.name: Military Retirement Pay State Income Tax Exemption
findings.description: Louisiana excludes federal retirement benefits, including military retired pay, from Louisiana taxable income under R.S. 47:44.2, which applies broadly to federal retirees (military and nonmilitary), with military survivor benefit plan payments also excludable. The Department of Revenue FAQ page fetched this session did not address whether VA disability compensation is separately exempt (VA disability compensation is not counted as gross income at the federal level to begin with, so it would generally not appear as Louisiana taxable income either, but this was not explicitly confirmed on the fetched page and should not be presented as a distinct, separately-legislated state exemption without further sourcing).
findings.value: 100% exclusion of military retired pay (and other federal retirement benefits) from Louisiana state income tax
otherReqs: Applies to federal retirees generally (military and nonmilitary) under R.S. 47:44.2
Federal military survivor benefit plan payments also excludable
findings.sourceExcerpt: Federal retirement benefits received by federal retirees, both military and nonmilitary, may be excluded from Louisiana taxable income... Federal benefits received from a military survivor benefit plan may also be excluded.
